newsitem.title: UK: INSTANT VIEW - UK JOBS, EARNINGS DATA, BOE MINUTES.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW - UK JOBS, EARNINGS DATA, BOE MINUTES.

text.p: Following is a selection of analysts' comments following release of British unemployment and average earnings data and minutes of a Bank of England meeting.

"It (the fall in unemployment) is bigger than expected and does indicate strength in the economy but underlying average earnings are unchanged... As long as there is an absence of wage pressure...the extent to which unemployment is falling is not going to be of concern to the markets."

"There's nothing there today which would cause great alarm, but looking ahead there are worrying developments. I'd focus on the continued strong falls in unemployment and more recently the turnaround in unit wage costs. If the Bank thinks 7.0 percent interest rates are going to be sufficient to bring inflation back down to target then it is sailing pretty close to the wind."

"Though the fall in unemployment at 49,000 was larger than had been anticipated, the ONS say that this may have been the result of seasonal problems. Average earnings were unchanged at 4.25 percent, suggesting no major upswing in wage pressures as yet.

"(In the BOE minutes), the BOE advice, a forecast of the quarterly inflation report later this morning, was that there was a risk of considerable increase in earnings and that the Bank was very concerned about the strength of money growth."

"So far the headlines we've got from the minutes look pretty bearish (for credit markets) as well (as the data)... I think people also think that if the pound wasn't there that possibly (rates) would've risen by 50 basis points.

"(Short sterling) has been selling off along with the gilt market. It's getting closer to realistic levels in my view. I think you've probably got further to go and the strip's very, very flat from December outwards."
